sequence_description: Direct JWT endpoint: control RS256 token succeeds, then attacker attempts alg=none token with same semantic claims (sub/aud/iss) to test signature bypass.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_alg_none_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted alg=none JWT; signature verification not bound to consumed proof (alg=none bypass)

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt kid header injection by signing with an attacker key and setting kid to a plausible trusted key id; should be rejected if Vault verifies against the correct trusted key set.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_kid_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_kid_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted attacker-signed JWT by trusting attacker-controlled kid header (signature verification policy mismatch)

sequence_description: Direct JWT login with config change: start with HTTPS JWKS trust, then downgrade jwks_url to HTTP and attempt attacker-signed token. Vault should not accept tokens validated via an insecure trust anchor (scheme downgrade).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_http_jwks_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_http_jwks_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted a token after JWKS URL scheme downgrade to HTTP, suggesting verification used an attacker-influenced trust anchor

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: simulate signing-key rotation by changing jwt_validation_pubkeys after a successful control login, then re-login with the SAME semantic claims but signed by the OLD key. If Vault still accepts the old-key token, verification policy is not applied to the consumed proof (stale trust set).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted a JWT signed by a removed/old key after trust-anchor rotation (stale verification policy applied to consumed proof)

sequence_description: Control login succeeds, then admin tightens role max_age; attacker replays the same JWT after the tighten to see if old token is still accepted beyond the new freshness window.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_A_replay_after_tighten_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_A_replay_after_tighten_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Replay of an old JWT (iat far older than new max_age) was accepted after freshness tightening; indicates stale freshness enforcement.

sequence_description: Admin attempts to enforce strict expiration by setting expiration_leeway=0 (sentinel default), then attacker uses a slightly expired token that may still be accepted due to default 150s leeway; includes a valid control and a second identity control.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_A_slightly_expired_attack_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_A_slightly_expired_attack_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Slightly expired JWT was accepted (likely due to leeway sentinel default behavior); freshness/anti-replay expectation violated for expired artifacts.

sequence_description: JWT trust-anchor rotation: baseline login with key-A succeeds; admin rotates jwt_validation_pubkeys to key-B; re-login with key-A must be rejected (no stale trust cache).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_rotA_reauth_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_rotA_reauth_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After rotating jwt_validation_pubkeys to key-B, Vault still accepted a JWT signed by key-A (stale trust cache / non-atomic config update)

sequence_description: Trust-anchor rotation coherence with two identities: baseline logins succeed under key-A. Admin rotates jwt_validation_pubkeys to key-B. New logins using key-A must be rejected for both identities (no stale trust cache).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_charlie_after_rotation_login_status >= 400 AND user_dana_after_rotation_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: (user_charlie_after_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False) AND (user_dana_after_rotation_login_status=200 >= 400 → False)
Implication: After rotating trusted keys, logins using the old signing key still succeeded, indicating stale trust cache or non-atomic config application

sequence_description: Case confusion: test whether sub='Admin' and sub='admin' collapse into the same Vault entity (case-folding bug in alias handling).
Empty/blank subject collision: test whether sub='' and sub=' ' (space) collapse into the same Vault entity due to trimming/normalization in alias handling.
description: Server returned HTTP 500 on login_with_jwt (auth_as=user_empty): ['missing name in alias']. Login endpoints must not return 5xx for any input.

sequence_description: Empty/blank subject collision: test whether sub='' and sub=' ' (space) collapse into the same Vault entity due to trimming/normalization in alias handling.
I4 attack: admin changes role identity_claim from 'sub' to 'email' between logins; attacker crafts JWT so two distinct principals map to same downstream entity after claim-switch.

Config-change attack: role initially bound to audience 'svc-low' (control success). Admin then loosens role to include 'svc-high'. Attacker re-authenticates with aud='svc-high' and attempts to read high secret. Secure behavior: access should still be denied unless explicitly granted by policy; role change should not accidentally attach high policy.
description: [PlatformVerify:vault] Audience bypass: sent=['svc-high'] not in configured=['svc-low']
